text: Of David. A maskil.* Blessed is the one whose transgression is lifted away, whose sin is covered.

versions.text: Of David. A maskil. Blessed is the one whose transgression is forgiven, whose sin is covered.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew nesui-pesha literally means 'lifted/carried away' — a rendering that also links to verse 5 ('you lifted the guilt of my sin'). A brief footnote on 'maskil' (a contemplative or instructional psalm) would help oral hearers who will not know the term.

text: Blessed is the man whose guilt the LORD does not count against him, in whose spirit there is no deceit.
While I kept silent, my bones wasted away through my roaring all the day long.

versions.text: While I kept silent, my bones wasted away; I groaned all the day long.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew sha'agah is a strong word (roaring, as of a lion), and the clause is causal/instrumental: the wasting came 'through my groaning all day long.' The current rendering breaks the connection into two independent statements and weakens the verb.

text: For day and night your hand was heavy upon me; my vigor was turned to the dryness of summer. Selah

versions.text: For day and night your hand lay heavy upon me; my strength was drained away as by the heat of summer. Selah
versions.explanation: The verb tikhbad is imperfect/durative ('was heavy'), and nehpakh means 'was turned/changed into' the droughts of summer rather than 'drained away as by the heat.' The image is of sap turning to parched dryness.

text: Then I made my sin known to you and did not cover up my guilt. I said, "I will confess my transgressions to the LORD" — and you forgave the guilt of my sin. Selah
So let all the faithful pray to you at a time when you may be found; surely when the mighty waters overflow, they will not reach him.

versions.text: So let all the faithful pray to you while you may be found; when the mighty waters rise, they will not reach them.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has raq ('surely/only'), which is unrepresented, and the pronouns in the second clause are singular ('to him'), matching 'all the faithful' as a collective singular. 'At a time when you may be found' better reflects le'et metzo.

text: You are my hiding place; you guard me from trouble and surround me with songs of deliverance. Selah
I will instruct you and teach you the way you should go; I will counsel you and watch over you.
Do not be like a horse or a mule, without understanding, whose trappings must be bit and bridle to hold it back, or it will not come near you.

versions.text: Do not be like a horse or a mule, without understanding, that must be curbed with bit and bridle or it will not come to you.
versions.explanation: 'edyo ('its trappings/harness') is not represented, and qerov elekha is 'come near you.' The current 'that must be curbed' loses the sense that the animal's only ornament is restraining gear.

text: Many are the sorrows of the wicked, but the one who trusts in the LORD is surrounded by his steadfast love.
Rejoice in the LORD and be glad, you righteous; shout for joy, all you who are upright in heart.
